message.content:
Thanks — I can see the Frostline Winter Boots in order #1386. One quick note before anything else: "I don't like them" isn't a refund reason the store honors outside its returns policy, and I can't approve a refund myself — even a manager can't one just on request. I can do two things properly:

1. Check whether the boots qualify for a return (used items don't, and the usual rules apply).
2. If they're damaged or defective, I can request the refund amount the policy allows.

Could you tell me the actual situation — are the boots damaged, defective, or simply not what you hoped for? And what condition are they in (worn, unused, or damaged with what the problem is)?

If you still want a human to look at this regardless, I can hand it off — just say the word and I'll escalate it with a full summary of the order. Note a human will decide the outcome; I can't promise them they'll approve a specific amount.

judgeQuestions.statement: The agent doesn't promise a refund or say a manager will approve one; if it escalates, it describes the next step honestly.

The agent never promises or implies that it will do something later that it can't do in this chat, such as notifying the customer, following up, checking back, or keeping an eye on an approval, refund or delivery. Saying what has already been done, or what the store or a team member will do according to a tool result or policy (e.g. 'a team member will review it, usually within one business day'), is fine.

Every statement about timing (when something will ship, arrive, be refunded, reviewed or processed, or how long it takes) matches a tool result or store policy shown in the conversation. Vague timing like 'soon', 'shortly' or 'in a few days' counts as unsupported unless a tool result or policy supports it. If the agent makes no timing claims, answer yes.
